prompt:
Use case: identity-preserve. Production animation extension of an ADOPTED pixel game character, not a redesign. The attached sheet is the approved design and poses at nearest 4x; use its first standing pose as exact identity, palette, scale and proportions. Same adopted lean black and tan Doberman, pointed upright ears, straight proud back/neck, angular muzzle, long thin legs, natural tail, slate highlights. No collar added. Standing body ~33 native pixels tall, larger than the already-adopted Shiba.
Create only these NEW motion poses: 4 columns x 3 rows, 12 distinct poses. Top row 4 alternating WALK phases with stable erect head/back and real leg changes. Middle row (4) gallop extension, (5) gathered gallop with all four legs tucked; (6) short forward biting lunge mouth open, (7) recover from bite mouth shut. Bottom row (8) alive hit flinch head tucks, (9) regain stance, (10) collapse gently onto side, (11) lying motionless on side with legs slack, closed eyes. The final two are non-graphic animal death (required by existing animal rules), no blood/wounds/bones. All facing RIGHT. No floating effects.
Transparent RGBA background, equal grid cells, generous transparent gutters, consistent full-body scale and ground baseline, complete feet and limbs. Clean chunky square pixel clusters for a small game sprite enlarged into the output, same muted palette, 1-pixel native dark brown contour, upper-left illumination. No smooth airbrushed illustration, no labels/grid/text/background/ground shadows/additional people. Same head and face in every cell. Meaningful limb changes, never just translated duplicates. Output only the motion sheet.
